title: Nuclear structure and notation; Rutherford scattering and atomic models
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: Q06-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; N01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; N01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; N01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: N01-1#N.3, Q06-1#N.4, N01-1#N.5, Q06-1#N.7a, N01-1#N.10, Q06-1#N.14a.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Nucleus
items.clue: Tiny positive core holding over 99.9% of the mass of an atom.

items.label: Nucleon number
items.clue: Symbol A: the total count of protons plus neutrons, 56 for iron-56.

items.label: Proton number
items.clue: Symbol Z: it fixes which element an atom is, 26 for every iron atom.

items.label: Neutron number
items.clue: Found as A – Z: 30 for iron-56, and 6, 7 or 8 for the three forms of carbon.

questions.stem: A nucleus of potassium-40 is written in nuclear notation as ⁴⁰₁₉K. Which statement about this nucleus is correct?
Predict first. Which statement about the results of the Geiger–Marsden–Rutherford alpha-particle scattering experiment is correct?

options.text: Most of the alpha particles were deflected through large angles, and only a few passed straight through.
Nearly all the alpha particles passed through almost undeflected; a very few were deflected by more than 90°.
The few alpha particles that bounced back had collided with the electrons in the gold atoms.
The few alpha particles that bounced back had struck the hard outer surface of a gold nucleus.

questions.stem: Predict first. Carbon-12 (¹²₆C) and carbon-14 (¹⁴₆C) are isotopes of carbon. Which statement about these two nuclides is correct?

options.text: They contain the same number of neutrons but different numbers of protons.
Both contain the same number of protons, but different numbers of neutrons.
Their atoms have different chemical properties, as their nuclei differ.
Their nuclei are identical, but their atoms have different numbers of electrons.

questions.stem: A gold nucleus has radius 7.0 × 10⁻¹⁵ m and a gold atom has radius 1.4 × 10⁻¹⁰ m. Roughly what fraction of the atom's volume does the nucleus occupy?
questions.explanation: (7.0 × 10⁻¹⁵ ÷ 1.4 × 10⁻¹⁰)³ = (5.0 × 10⁻⁵)³ = 1.25 × 10⁻¹³. The atom is almost entirely empty space.

questions.stem: Which pair are isotopes of the same element?
A gold nucleus is about 1.4 × 10⁻¹⁴ m across and a gold atom is about 2.9 × 10⁻¹⁰ m across. In a scale drawing the nucleus is a dot 1 mm across. How wide must the atom be drawn?
